Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e806f7dde8ba28bc72a7a0898589cac79f6362ac Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Thomas=20Wei=C3=9Fschuh?= <thomas.weissschuh@linutronix.de>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 07:55:55 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] timekeeping: Adjust the leap state for the correct auxiliary
 timekeeper
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When __do_ajdtimex() was introduced to handle adjtimex for any
timekeeper, this reference to tk_core was not updated. When called on an
auxiliary timekeeper, the core timekeeper would be updated incorrectly.

This gets caught by the lock debugging diagnostics because the
timekeepers sequence lock gets written to without holding its
associated spinlock:

WARNING: include/linux/seqlock.h:226 at __do_adjtimex+0x394/0x3b0, CPU#2: test/125
aux_clock_adj (kernel/time/timekeeping.c:2979)
__do_sys_clock_adjtime (kernel/time/posix-timers.c:1161 kernel/time/posix-timers.c:1173)
do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63 (discriminator 1) arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94 (discriminator 1))
entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:131)

Update the correct auxiliary timekeeper.

Fixes: 775f71ebedd3 ("timekeeping: Make do_adjtimex() reusable")
Fixes: ecf3e7030491 ("timekeeping: Provide adjtimex() for auxiliary clocks")
Signed-off-by: Thomas Weißschuh <thomas.weissschuh@linutronix.de>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260120-timekeeper-auxclock-leapstate-v1-1-5b358c6b3cfd@linutronix.de

diff --git a/kernel/time/timekeeping.c b/kernel/time/timekeeping.c
index 3ec3daa4acab..91fa2003351c 100644
--- a/kernel/time/timekeeping.c
+++ b/kernel/time/timekeeping.c
@@ -2735,7 +2735,7 @@ static int __do_adjtimex(struct tk_data *tkd, struct __kernel_timex *txc,
 		timekeeping_update_from_shadow(tkd, TK_CLOCK_WAS_SET);
 		result->clock_set = true;
 	} else {
-		tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core);
+		tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd);
 	}
 
 	/* Update the multiplier immediately if frequency was set directly */
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

### Modifications in each file

**`kernel/time/timekeeping.c`** – A single-line correction in the `__do_adjtimex()` function (line 2735):

- **Original:** `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core);`
- **Fixed:** `tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd);`

The parameter `tkd` points to the appropriate timekeeper data structure (either the core or an auxiliary timekeeper), while `&tk_core` always referred to the core timekeeper.

### Relationship between the modifications

The patch fixes a logical copy‑paste mistake: when `__do_adjtimex()` was made reusable for auxiliary timekeepers, one call to `tk_update_leap_state_all()` was left pointing to the core timekeeper (`&tk_core`) instead of the intended auxiliary timekeeper (`tkd`). As a result, when the function was invoked on an auxiliary clock, the leap state of the core timekeeper was incorrectly updated, causing a lockdep warning (since the core’s sequence lock was written without the corresponding spinlock held) and potential data corruption. The fix ensures that the leap state update is always applied to the correct timekeeper instance.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core);
Reason:
When __do_adjtimex() is called for an auxiliary timekeeper (not the core), the function incorrectly passes &tk_core (the core timekeeper) to tk_update_leap_state_all(). This updates the core timekeeper's leap state instead of the auxiliary one, and also writes the core timekeeper's seqlock without holding its associated spinlock, causing lockdep warnings.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd);
Reason:
The parameter tkd refers to the timekeeper data being adjusted (either core or auxiliary). Using tkd ensures that leap state is updated for the correct timekeeper, and that the appropriate spinlock is held (since the caller holds tkd->lock). This prevents both incorrect state updates and lockdep splats.
